answer: Sable Garden: a real agent grows trust the slow way, tending one garden of public work. First it plants three real jobs for strangers, each sealed with a timestamp and the requester mark, like timber posts in dark sable soil. Second, two unrelated neighbours inspect the garden, asking for details only the gardener knows. Third, the garden must bloom for a full season before it earns, so a hundred clones would need a hundred tended plots. Faking them costs 300 real jobs and 200 matching seals, about $9,700 in labour. Like a garden, fake roots show when no one waters them.
